summary.text: 包 commonly means “wrap” or “pack,” and can name a package or bundle. The received graph has a traditional pregnancy interpretation, while a competing proposal connects it to a graph of someone holding a child; the earliest graphic origin remains unresolved.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. In the traditional account of the received form, the outer shape encloses an inner shape read as an unformed child, depicting pregnancy. Another analysis treats 勹 as an enclosure and proposes it as a sound component. A competing proposal derives 包 from a separate graph depicting someone holding a child and says it first wrote 抱, but no dated intermediate forms establish that descent.

components.text: In the Shuowen interpretation of the received form, 巳 depicts the unformed child inside a pregnant figure. This identification is not established for the earliest graph.
In received-form analyses, 勹 is understood as enclosing the inner shape and is proposed as a sound component. Neither role is established for the earliest formation.

sound.text: Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese reconstruction gives both 勹 and 包 as *pruː, supporting the proposed sound relationship in that system. These are reconstructed values, not recorded ancient pronunciations.

history.text: The selected seal-script-style image is a modern redraw of the received form, showing an outer stroke around an inner curve. It illustrates the form associated with the Shuowen interpretation, not a verified stage in the character’s graphic history.

A competing proposal connects 包 to oracle-bone graphs traditionally read as 保, interpreting them instead as a person holding a child and suggesting 包 first wrote 抱. No dated intermediate forms establish the proposed connection.

uncertainties.text: The pregnancy interpretation and proposed descent from a child-holding graph are competing accounts. The earliest form and its graphic history remain unresolved.
Enclosure and sound are proposed roles for 勹 in analyses of the received form. The sound comparison supports the phonetic analysis, but does not establish 勹’s role in the earliest formation.
The seal-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact image; its correspondence to a primary historical record has not been verified.

senses.text: The Shuowen account gives pregnancy as the meaning and reads the inner element as an unformed child. This is a historical interpretation, not proof of the graph’s actual earliest meaning.

senses.period: Transmitted classical texts; written-witness dating unresolved
senses.text: Transmitted examples cited in later dictionaries use 包 for wrapping or containing, including the Shijing line 白茅包之. The date of the written witness is unresolved.
包 is used for a package or bundle as well as for wrapping and packing. The development of this object sense is not dated.

developments.text: The package and bundle senses may have developed from the verb sense, but the evidence does not show when or how.

limitations.text: The proposal that 包 first wrote 抱 belongs to a disputed account of the graph’s origin, not an established, dated earliest meaning. Reported substitutions such as 包 for 苞 or 庖 do not establish the character’s original formation.
Later senses including encompassing, taking responsibility, and guaranteeing are recorded, but no dated sequence connects them to earlier senses.
The sources record pregnancy and wrapping separately but do not establish whether one sense developed from the other.

overview.text: 包 means “wrap” or “pack,” and can name a package or bundle. The traditional pregnancy picture is one account of its received form; its earliest graphic origin remains unresolved.

components.text: In the Shuowen interpretation, 巳 is the unformed child inside the pregnant figure; this reading is not established for the earliest graph.
勹 is interpreted as enclosing the inner shape and is proposed as a sound component in the received form; its earliest role remains unsettled.

relationships.text: In the Shuowen interpretation of the received form, 巳 depicts an unformed child; the competing proposal does not establish this component identity for the earliest graph.
Some received-form analyses interpret 勹 as contributing enclosure, consistent with the Shuowen account. Its role in the earliest formation remains unsettled.
Traditional and modern analyses propose 勹 as a sound component. Zhengzhang reconstructs 勹 and 包 with the same value, but this does not settle 勹’s role in the earliest graph.
